identity_evidence.quote: A 31-year-old man underwent pars plana vitrectomy for traumatic retinal detachment

attribution_limitations: The introduction defines SJS/TEN overlap as 10%-30% BSA with epidermal detachment and TEN as >30%, while the case reports epidermal detachment over 80% and BSA involvement >30% and still confirms SJS/TEN overlap syndrome.

The abstract reports 99% of total body surface area involved by erythema, bullae, epidermal detachment and erosions, while the body text reports initial epidermal detachment of 20% progressing to over 80% within 24 hours; the abstract does not say whether 99% refers to detachment alone or to all lesions; 99% is numerically consistent with over 80% and >30%, so this is recorded as an ambiguity about what the figure measures, not as a source conflict.
Table 1 prints two (1-3)-β-D-glucan values with dates (August 24 and September 2) under the column header On admission; the text only says the glucan was significantly elevated.
The text says visual acuity improved to 0.05 after penetrating keratoplasty without naming the eye in that clause; the left eye had the keratoplasty indication in the same sentence.

The text states that brinzolamide was initiated and that the reaction developed on day 6 of use, but does not state when or whether brinzolamide was stopped; Naranjo criterion 3 (improvement on discontinuation) is scored +1 in Table 2.
The text speculates that the left eye damage exceeded the treated right eye possibly due to local tissue susceptibility or immunologic factors; this is an author hypothesis.
The abstract says cutaneous lesions resolved over 4 weeks, while the case text says the skin lesions had largely healed by week 4 with residual hyperpigmentation and scarring.
High-sensitivity CRP is printed as >5.00 mg/L with a reference range of 0-10 mg/L while the text groups it with elevated inflammatory markers.
The stool Gram stain sentence cites Table 1, but Table 1 has no stool Gram stain row.
